examples: I drink tea in the morning.
우리 같이 차 한 잔 마셔요.
Let us drink a cup of tea together.
nuance: 차 is a drink, so it takes 마셔요 (drink), not 먹어요 (eat). The same sound 차 can also mean a car, so context tells them apart.
mistakes: Using 먹어요 instead of 마셔요 with 차

examples: I want to drink orange juice.
nuance: 주스 is a drink and takes 마셔요 (drink), never 먹어요 (eat). Add a fruit word like 오렌지 in front to name the flavor you mean.
mistakes: Using 먹어요 instead of 마셔요 with 주스

nuance: 콜라 is a fizzy drink, so it takes 마셔요 (drink), not 먹어요 (eat). It usually means any cola brand, much like the English word.
mistakes: Using 먹어요 instead of 마셔요 with 콜라

examples: I drink beer in the evening.
I want to drink beer with chicken.
nuance: 맥주 is a drink, so it takes 마셔요 (drink), not 먹어요 (eat). Koreans often pair 맥주 with fried chicken in a combo called chimaek.
mistakes: Using 먹어요 instead of 마셔요 with 맥주

examples: This soju is a bit strong.
Today I want to drink soju.
nuance: 소주 is a popular Korean liquor and takes 마셔요 (drink), not 먹어요 (eat). It is usually shared in small glasses, and pouring for others is polite.
mistakes: Using 먹어요 instead of 마셔요 with 소주

examples: This wine is a bit expensive.
I want to drink wine tonight.
nuance: 와인 is a drink, so it takes 마셔요 (drink), not 먹어요 (eat). Red wine is 레드 와인 and white wine is 화이트 와인 in everyday speech.
mistakes: Using 먹어요 instead of 마셔요 with 와인

usage: I want to drink green tea
examples: I drink green tea after meals.
This green tea is very warm.
I want to drink green tea.
nuance: 녹차 means green tea and takes 마셔요 (drink), not 먹어요 (eat). The word literally combines green and tea, so the color tells you the type.
mistakes: Using 먹어요 instead of 마셔요 with 녹차

examples: I buy bottled water at the convenience store.
This bottled water is very cool.
nuance: 생수 is packaged drinking water and takes 마셔요 (drink), not 먹어요 (eat). It is the bottled kind you buy, unlike plain tap water called 물.
mistakes: Using 먹어요 instead of 마셔요 with 생수

usage: I want to drink sparkling water
examples: I drink sparkling water with meals.
This sparkling water is really cool.
I want to drink sparkling water.
nuance: 탄산수 is fizzy water and takes 마셔요 (drink), not 먹어요 (eat). The word means carbonated water, so it has bubbles unlike plain 물.
mistakes: Using 먹어요 instead of 마셔요 with 탄산수

usage: I want to drink a beverage
examples: I drink a beverage at lunch.
What beverage do you want to drink?
nuance: 음료수 is a general word for any cold drink and takes 마셔요 (drink), not 먹어요 (eat). It usually means soft drinks rather than water or alcohol.
mistakes: Using 먹어요 instead of 마셔요 with 음료수

examples: I put ice in the water.
nuance: 얼음 is frozen water that you add to drinks, so you put it in rather than drink it. With 얼음 use 넣어요 (put in), and 마셔요 stays for the drink itself.
mistakes: Using 마셔요 with 얼음 instead of 넣어요

examples: I want to drink sikhye after the sauna.
nuance: 식혜 is a sweet traditional rice drink and takes 마셔요 (drink), not 먹어요 (eat). Koreans enjoy it cold on holidays and often at saunas.
mistakes: Using 먹어요 instead of 마셔요 with 식혜
